title: Feature chain
lede: How a feature idea becomes a reviewed, tested PR. The owner decides intent and merges; the agent does the rest.

design.name: Design
design.role: Agree on what to build and why, one question at a time.
details: The agent explores the code first and only asks what the code can't answer, each time with a recommended answer.

more: Decisions with rationale, canonical vocabulary, edge cases.

qs: What makes a design question worth asking the owner instead of deciding?

prd.name: PRD
prd.role: Turn the design into user stories and testing decisions, without re-interviewing.
details: Cross-checks the design against the codebase and names which modules need tests.

tdd.name: TDD slices
tdd.role: Build in thin vertical slices: failing test, minimal code, refactor, commit.
details: Granularity is confirmed once with the owner; after that, slices run without pausing.
risks: Writing all tests first verifies imagined behavior; one test at a time keeps them honest.

refine.name: Refine
refine.role: Two independent reviewers (correctness, structure) report; one pass applies every fix.
details: A test weakened to pass counts as a defect, not a fix.

qa.name: QA
qa.role: Run the real app and drive the changed entry points the way a user would.

review.name: Owner review
review.role: A summary and a PR; the owner reviews and merges.
details: Merging needs explicit owner authorization; a PR is not approval.

prd.d: Product requirements document: the problem, solution and user stories.

slice.d: A thin piece of a feature that cuts through every layer and ships working on its own.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand scaffold's feature chain: how an AI agent takes a feature from idea to reviewed PR.
